source.agency: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: PLACES: County Data (GIS Friendly Format), 2025 release

measures.label: Adults lacking reliable transportation
measures.definition: Transportation prevented medical appointments, meetings, work or obtaining daily essentials.

measures.label: Adults experiencing food insecurity
measures.definition: Food ran out at least sometimes and there was insufficient money to buy more.

measures.label: Adults experiencing housing insecurity
measures.definition: Unable to pay mortgage, rent or a utility bill.

measures.label: Adults facing a utility shutoff threat
measures.definition: An electricity, gas, oil or water company threatened to discontinue service.

measures.label: Adults with any disability
measures.definition: At least one of the six disability types covered by the BRFSS questions.

interpretation: All seven selected measures use 2023 estimates from the 2025 release. The release year and retrieval date are not observation years.
Values are model-based crude prevalence estimates, not age-adjusted prevalence and not direct local survey estimates.
Uninsured covers adults aged 18–64. The other selected indicators cover adults aged 18 or older. Do not combine their denominators.
These are community estimates, not SozoRock program results or individual needs. They do not establish waiting times, causation, program impact or eligibility.
Do not multiply the uninsured percentage by the dataset total adult population because the eligible population differs.
Transportation covers medical appointments and other daily activities; it does not mean medical-appointment failure alone.
Utility services threat describes a threatened shutoff, not necessarily a completed shutoff.
The current CDC release notes rename social isolation as feelings of loneliness. The GIS schema retains older social-isolation wording; use the current measure name and definition.
recommendedPublicSourceLine: Source: CDC PLACES, 2025 release. Model-based crude estimates for 2023, with 95% confidence intervals. Retrieved October 20, 2026. These county estimates describe community conditions, not SozoRock results or individual needs. Health insurance covers ages 18–64; the other measures cover adults aged 18 or older.
